newsitem.title: CHINA: China economic tsar seen in public after illness.
newsitem.headline: China economic tsar seen in public after illness.

text.p: China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji, after cancelling weekend meetings due to illness, attended a meeting of parliament's advisory body on Wednesday.
Vice-Premier Zhu was seen by reporters at the closing session of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in Beijing.
Zhu, 68, cancelled meetings with visiting British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and International Monetary Fund chief Michel Camdessus on Saturday due to ill health, diplomats said.
They said they had been told that China's chief economic strategist had been taken to hospital with influenza or light pneumonia. Chinese government officials made no comment on his health.

Zhu has been instrumental in pushing for a rebuilding of the central government's economic power, much of it relinquished to regional authorities in the early days of reform in a bid to spur development. He has also been a key figure in promoting greater regulation of the nation's financial markets.
